notes.h: Nodal regions and the idea of a node
notes.b: A nodal region is a city together with the surrounding area linked to it by flows of people, goods, services and information. It is defined by connections, not by uniform features.
points: A node is a central point where routes meet by road, rail, sea or air, usually a town or city.
A nodal region is also called a functional, city or urban region.
A hinterland is the area around a town or city that it serves and depends on for jobs, shopping, services and markets. It is also called its sphere of influence or urban field.
The urban area is the continuously built-up part of the city; the hinterland extends far beyond it.
The commuter belt is the part of the hinterland from which people travel daily to work in the city.

notes.h: How a city and its hinterland interact
points: Jobs: commuters travel in from the hinterland every day.
Services: the city provides shops, hospitals, third-level colleges, entertainment and offices that smaller places cannot support, and people from the hinterland travel in to use them.
Goods: the hinterland supplies food, water, raw materials and labour; the city supplies manufactured goods and services.
A port's hinterland is the area whose trade passes through it.
Information: local newspapers, radio and TV stations serve the hinterland.
Commuting data from the census show where people travel to work.
The catchment area of a hospital, college or secondary school.
The circulation area of a local newspaper, or the reach of a local radio station.
Bus and rail routes and timetables.
The delivery areas of businesses, and the home addresses of shoppers or of members of a sports club.
The edge of a hinterland is not a sharp line: neighbouring hinterlands overlap, and different services give different boundaries.
Larger cities have larger hinterlands; a capital city's hinterland for some services is the whole country.
Motorways, car ownership, faster rail and remote working extend commuter belts outwards.
New shopping centres or services in smaller towns can shrink a city's hinterland.

notes.h: Dublin: a primate city and its hinterland
notes.b: A primate city is the largest city in a country, far larger than any other. Dublin is Ireland's primate city and capital.
points: It is the focus of the national motorway network: radial routes meet at the M50 ring road. The main rail lines also meet there.
Dublin Port and Dublin Airport, Ireland's busiest airport, make the city the main national gateway for trade and travel.
The commuter belt extends into Meath, Kildare, Wicklow and Louth, with fast-growing commuter towns: Navan (Co. Meath), Naas and Newbridge (Co. Kildare), Bray (Co. Wicklow) and Drogheda (Co. Louth).
For government, national media, specialist hospitals and the main airport, Dublin's hinterland is the whole country.
Problems of its urban region: urban sprawl, long commutes and congestion, and high house prices.
The growth of city regions and Dublin's council structures are covered in the European Regions chapter; land use and planning are covered in the Urban Geography chapter.
Cork: Ireland's second city, at the head of Cork Harbour on the River Lee.
Cork Harbour has a port and a pharmaceutical industry, with plants at Ringaskiddy. Cork's hinterland covers much of Munster, with commuter towns Carrigaline, Midleton and Cobh.
Galway: the main city of the West, serving a large rural hinterland that includes Connemara.
Galway is a centre of the medical devices industry and of higher education, home to the University of Galway.
Limerick and Waterford are regional cities serving the Mid-West and the South-East.

notes.h: Planning to balance Irish city regions
points: The National Planning Framework, part of Project Ireland 2040 and published in 2018, aims to direct more growth to Cork, Limerick, Galway and Waterford to counterbalance Dublin.
Paris is the primate city of France, at the centre of the Paris Basin. Radial motorways and TGV high-speed lines meet there, so its hinterland reaches across France.
The first TGV line, Paris to Lyon, opened in 1981. Charles de Gaulle Airport serves the city.

London is the capital of the United Kingdom and a global financial centre, through the City of London. Greater London has about 9 million people (Census 2021), and its commuter belt covers much of south-east England.

Brussels is the capital of Belgium and seat of the main EU institutions: the European Commission, the Council of the EU and the European Parliament, which also meets in Strasbourg. NATO headquarters is also in Brussels.
Rotterdam is Europe's largest port, at the mouth of the Rhine (Europoort). Its hinterland is the whole Rhine basin, linked by river barges, rail and pipelines, so it crosses national borders.
Milan is the main city of Lombardy, the core of northern Italy, and Italy's financial centre, home to the Borsa Italiana stock exchange.
Other urban regions named in exam matching include Munich (capital of Bavaria), Berlin (capital of Germany) and Rome (capital of Italy).

notes.h: The Randstad: a polycentric city region
points: The Randstad in the Netherlands is a ring of cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) forming one large urban region around a rural area called the Green Heart (Groene Hart).
It is polycentric, with many centres, in contrast to the single-centre city regions of Paris and Dublin.

keyTerms.definition: A central point where transport routes meet, usually a town or city.
A city and the surrounding area linked to it by flows of people, goods, services and information.
The area around a town or city that it serves and depends on for jobs, shopping, services and markets.
The part of a city's hinterland from which people travel daily to work in the city.
The continuously built-up part of a city.
The largest city in a country, far larger than any other, usually the capital.
A city region with several centres of similar size rather than one dominant city.

questions.prompt: Examine the relationship between an urban area and its hinterland, with reference to an Irish or European city you have studied.
questions.model: Dublin is a nodal region: a primate city linked by flows to the surrounding area. Its urban area is the built-up city, while its hinterland extends far beyond it. Its node status comes from radial national routes meeting at the M50 ring road, the main rail lines, Dublin Port and Dublin Airport. The commuter belt extends into Meath, Kildare, Wicklow and Louth, with commuter towns such as Navan, Naas, Newbridge, Bray and Drogheda. Flows run both ways: commuters travel in to jobs, while the hinterland supplies food, water, raw materials and labour, and the city supplies manufactured goods and services. The city provides shops, hospitals, third-level colleges, entertainment and offices that smaller places cannot support. For government, national media, specialist hospitals and the main airport, the hinterland is the whole country. The hinterland is measured by commuting census data, the catchment areas of hospitals and colleges, the circulation area of local newspapers, bus and rail routes, business delivery areas and the home addresses of shoppers. Its edge is not sharp, because neighbouring hinterlands overlap. It changes over time: motorways, car ownership, faster rail and remote working extend commuter belts. The relationship also brings problems, including urban sprawl, long commutes and congestion, and high house prices.

questions.prompt: Explain what is meant by a nodal region and describe one way the extent of a city's hinterland can be measured.
questions.model: A nodal region is a city together with the surrounding area linked to it by flows of people, goods, services and information, so it is defined by connections rather than by uniform features. One way to measure the hinterland is by the catchment area of a hospital, college or secondary school, which shows the area from which its users come. Other methods include commuting data from the census and the circulation area of a local newspaper.

questions.prompt: True or false: (a) A city's hinterland can be mapped using the circulation area of its local newspaper. (b) A nodal region is defined by features that are the same throughout it.
questions.model: (a) True: the circulation area of a local newspaper shows the area the city's media serves. (b) False: a nodal region is defined by links to a central node, not by features that are the same throughout it.
